questions.prompt: Why does the classic momentum score skip the latest month?
options: The latest month's prices are not known yet at the end of the month
Returns over the most recent month tend to partly reverse, which works against the longer pattern
Leaving out one month lowers transaction costs
A 12-month window is too long for pandas to shift
questions.explanation: Short-term returns tend to partly reverse within about a month, while 3 to 12 month returns tend to continue. Skipping the latest month keeps the two effects apart.

questions.prompt: A stock was at 50 twelve months ago, 60 one month ago and 54 today. What is its 12-1 momentum score?
questions.explanation: The score uses the price 1 month ago and the price 12 months ago: 60 / 50 - 1 = 0.20. Today's price of 54 falls in the skipped month, so it does not count.

questions.prompt: What risk of momentum did Daniel and Moskowitz (2016) document?
options: Rare, very large losses when the market rebounds fast after a fall and past losers rise most
Steady small losses every month that cancel the average gain
Losses only when the market rises slowly
No risk, because a momentum factor portfolio is market-neutral
questions.explanation: They named these losses momentum crashes. The short side holds past losers, so a fast rebound that lifts those losers most hits the portfolio hard.
